structure.title: Suspicion at court
structure.text: The first movement follows Leontes' interpretation of an apparently friendly encounter and the authority he gives it.

structure.title: Time and another generation
structure.text: A major passage of years changes the play's setting and tone. The earlier actions remain active within new relationships.

people.text: His old friend and a visiting king.

context.title: Certainty without agreement
context.text: Leontes treats his interpretation as evident even when others contradict it. Royal authority makes that private conviction consequential.

context.title: A romance's changing tone
context.text: The play moves between severe accusation, pastoral comedy, and wonder. The change of register does not simply cancel what preceded it.
context.takeaway: Let the parts remain in tension.

notice.why: Speaking plainly can require courage under a suspicious ruler.

notice.why: Repair involves more than retracting a statement.

opening: Leontes watches his wife persuade his oldest friend to prolong a visit and decides they must be lovers. Almost everyone around him sees an innocent exchange. Their objections only make him more certain that he alone understands what is happening. Shakespeare begins with the frightening speed of a private suspicion becoming public policy, then gives the consequences room to stretch across years. The play asks an unusual amount of time, affection, and imagination from the people left trying to live after a powerful man's certainty.
